title: Throwing Mechanics & Arm Care Lessons in Long Beach & OC | MBM
description: Private throwing lessons with Coach Myles — clean arm action, accuracy, and velocity built on healthy, arm-care-first mechanics. Ages 8–18, Long Beach & Orange County.
lead: Every throw on the field starts with the same thing: clean, repeatable arm action. Coach Myles teaches throwing the healthy way — accuracy and velocity built on sound mechanics and arm care, so players throw harder without throwing themselves into trouble.
body: Throwing is a full-body movement, not an arm movement. Coach Myles works on the footwork and direction to the target, the glove side, a clean and efficient arm path, and a balanced follow-through. When the body lines up and the sequence repeats, accuracy follows — and velocity becomes a byproduct of clean mechanics and a strong, well-cared-for arm rather than something a young player muscles up for.

Arm care comes first, always. Proper warm-up routines, sensible throwing programs, and real respect for workload and rest keep young arms healthy, in line with MLB Pitch Smart guidelines for youth pitchers. Long-toss and velocity work have their place, but only once mechanics are clean and the arm is prepared for it.

These fundamentals serve every player on the field. Position players get more accurate and more durable; pitchers build on the same foundation with mound-specific work. The order of operations is the same for everyone: clean mechanics and accuracy first, then let strength and velocity come as the athlete grows.

faq.q: How do you protect young arms?
faq.a: Arm care comes first — proper warm-ups, sensible workloads, and rest, following MLB Pitch Smart guidelines. We build durability before chasing velocity.

faq.q: Can throwing mechanics really add velocity?
faq.a: Over time, yes — safely. Velocity is a byproduct of clean mechanics and strength that develops as the athlete grows, never something we force at a young arm's expense.
